A mine is a hole holding up a mountain - and the rock is always trying to close it. Here is why mines fail.

#shorts #engineering #science #mining #howitworks

sahneler.metin: A mine is a hole holding up millions of tons of rock.
When it fails, the roof can crush everything in seconds.
But what actually holds it up?
Miners leave pillars of rock to hold up the roof.
Take out too much, and those pillars slowly crush.
One failing pillar can start a chain collapse.
Water seeping in weakens the rock and rusts the supports.
Modern mines listen for the rock groaning before it gives way.

vaka.yanilgi: Mine roofs rarely fail without warning — rock often cracks and pops as the load shifts.
